step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 52-year-old female presenting with an ulcerative forearm nodule suspected of CL

step5_concept_grounding: Cutaneous leishmaniasis (ruled out) in favor of small lymphocytic lymphoma / leukemia cutis

evidence_items.source_quote: The skin lesion was initially suspected of being cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) because of its endemism in our country. However, the microscopic examination of the Giemsa-stained smears of skin lesion was negative.
The histopathological examination of the biopsy specimen showed a dense, diffuse, and monomorphous infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis, which rejected the diagnosis of CL.
Finally, the lesion was diagnosed as leukemia cutis (involving stage I of SLL/CLL).
evidence_items.target_concept: Alternative diagnosis: leukemia cutis / small lymphocytic lymphoma

rationale: A 52-year-old female had an ulcerative forearm nodule clinically suspected of cutaneous leishmaniasis. Giemsa-stained smears and histopathological examination were negative and rejected CL, establishing an alternative diagnosis of leukemia cutis (SLL/CLL stage I) responsive to rituximab. Leishmaniasis is explicitly ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 3-year-old female with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and reactive granulomatous dermatitis.

evidence_items.source_quote: Special stains did not reveal any infectious organisms. Bacterial, fungal, and acid-fast tissue cultures were negative. Due to the rarity of leishmaniasis and leprosy in her geographic area, absence of travel history, and lack of specific features on pathology, additional specialty microbiologic testing was not performed.
evidence_items.test_name: Histopathology special stains and clinico-epidemiological exclusion

step12_audit.primary_case_diagnosis: Reactive granulomatous dermatitis in acute lymphoblastic leukemia

rationale: A 3-year-old girl on maintenance chemotherapy for ALL presented with ulcerated papules and nodules on her extremities showing palisading granulomas on skin biopsy. Special stains revealed no infectious organisms, and leishmaniasis was excluded based on lack of histopathologic features, absence of travel history, and geographic rarity, establishing reactive granulomatous dermatitis -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 56-year-old man with untreated HIV/AIDS presenting with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and disseminated Cryptococcus neoformans infection.

evidence_items.source_quote: Additional serologic studies for syphilis, Toxoplasma gondii, Leishmania, and Hepatitis B and C virus were negative.

step12_audit.primary_case_diagnosis: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and disseminated Cryptococcus neoformans coinfection in HIV/AIDS

rationale: A 56-year-old man with untreated HIV/AIDS (CD4 1 cell/uL) was admitted with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and disseminated cryptococcosis (Cryptococcus neoformans in BAL, blood, and CSF). Serologic testing for Leishmania was explicitly negative. Assertion NEGATED, clinical role RULED_OUT_DIAGNOSIS -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 45-year-old male chef with a microcystic adnexal carcinoma (MAC) plaque on the right forearm.

evidence_items.source_quote: Basidiobolomycosis, sarcoidosis, and leishmaniasis were considered as differential diagnoses, and an incisional biopsy was done and sent for histopathological examination. The pathologist's initial report was suggestive of syringoma, however, this did not correlate with the clinical presentation, further revaluation of the slide was done and a final diagnosis of MAC was concluded.

step12_audit.primary_case_diagnosis: Microcystic adnexal carcinoma (MAC)

rationale: A 45-year-old male presented with a solitary indurated plaque on the right forearm present for 20 years. Leishmaniasis was considered in the clinical differential diagnosis, and incisional biopsy histopathology with S100 immunohistochemistry established microcystic adnexal carcinoma (MAC), ruling out leishmaniasis -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 35-year-old Congolese female with hepatic and pulmonary sarcoidosis and vanishing bile duct syndrome.

evidence_items.source_quote: Mycobacterium tuberculosis work-up was negative, and the hepatic granuloma etiological study was negative for syphilis, toxoplasmosis, rubella, leptospirosis, Q fever, Schistosoma, brucella, leishmaniasis and histoplasmosis.

step12_audit.primary_case_diagnosis: Hepatic and pulmonary sarcoidosis with vanishing bile duct syndrome

rationale: A 35-year-old Congolese woman presented with cholestatic jaundice, pruritus, weight loss, and non-caseating bronchial and hepatic granulomas with vanishing bile duct syndrome. Etiological testing for leishmaniasis was explicitly negative, and hepatic and pulmonary sarcoidosis was diagnosed. Assertion NEGATED, clinical role RULED_OUT_DIAGNOSIS -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 70-year-old male (Patient 3 of a 4-patient case series) diagnosed with eosinophilic fasciitis.

evidence_items.source_quote: The etiological workup revealed negative parasite serologies (Strongyloides, Echinococcus, Fasciola, Toxocara, Leishmania), negative stool parasitology, and negative immune tests for antinuclear antibodies and anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies.

step12_audit.primary_case_diagnosis: Eosinophilic fasciitis

rationale: A 70-year-old man presented with asthenia, fever, bilateral limb edema, marked peripheral eosinophilia, and skin thickening, and was diagnosed by full-thickness biopsy with eosinophilic fasciitis. Parasite serology for Leishmania was explicitly negative. Assertion NEGATED, clinical role RULED_OUT_DIAGNOSIS -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 41-year-old Egyptian woman from Al Fayoum with suspected seronegative celiac disease and massive splenomegaly.

evidence_items.source_quote: Infectious screening, including hepatitis B and C, HIV, EBV, CMV, Brucella, and Leishmania serologies, was negative (Table 6).

Histological examination of duodenal and jejunal biopsies showed preserved villous architecture with a mild increase in intraepithelial lymphocytes (50-60 per 100 enterocytes), consistent with Marsh I-II changes. No parasites, granulomas, dysplasia, or malignant features were observed.

step12_audit.primary_case_diagnosis: Suspected seronegative celiac disease with massive splenomegaly

rationale: A 41-year-old Egyptian woman presented with chronic diarrhea, severe electrolyte derangements, and massive splenomegaly (25 cm), and was diagnosed with seronegative celiac disease responsive to a gluten-free diet. Leishmania serology was explicitly negative, and duodenal/jejunal and bone marrow biopsies showed no parasites. Assertion NEGATED, clinical role RULED_OUT_DIAGNOSIS -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 19-year-old male from Sao Tome and Principe with primary extracranial parieto-occipital Ewing sarcoma.

evidence_items.source_quote: Bacterial, fungal, and parasitic cultures, as well as PCR for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, nontuberculous mycobacteria, and pan-fungal targets, were negative, as was Leishmania testing.

step12_audit.primary_case_diagnosis: Primary extracranial Ewing sarcoma (EWSR1-rearranged)

rationale: A 19-year-old man from Sao Tome and Principe presented with a large ulcerated, bleeding parieto-occipital mass confirmed by histopathology, CD99 positivity, and EWSR1 rearrangement as primary extracranial Ewing sarcoma. Parasitic cultures and Leishmania testing on the mass biopsy were explicitly negative. Assertion NEGATED, clinical role RULED_OUT_DIAGNOSIS -> NEGATIVE.
